title: High-Voltage Rack Power
_authoring: Authored 2026-06-20 (L4), factual content; references OCP/industry practice, no fabricated DOIs. Conservative evidence; quantitative figures left sparse where not certain.

activations.domainDescription: Open Compute Project 48 V DC rack power bus distributes power down the rack at higher voltage, cutting current and busbar losses versus 12 V.
activations.domainFunction: Delivers rack power at 48 V so per-watt current and resistive loss drop, enabling higher-density racks.
activations.whyThisNode: M1 is the final motor-output stage; the 48 V bus is the final power-delivery stage into the rack.

companies.name: Vertiv
companies.functional_reason: Rack power shelves and 48 V power delivery products.

activations.domainDescription: Higher-voltage DC distribution (e.g. ±400 V DC) to the rack is an emerging approach to reduce conversion stages and copper; still early in deployment.
activations.domainFunction: Routes power to racks as DC at high voltage, removing AC/DC conversion steps along the chain.
activations.whyThisNode: The corpus callosum is the high-bandwidth routing tract; HVDC is the high-voltage routing of power to the rack.

companies.name: Eaton
companies.functional_reason: DC power distribution and conversion equipment.

activations.domainDescription: Each AC/DC and DC/DC conversion loses a few percent; minimizing stages from utility feed to chip raises end-to-end efficiency.
activations.domainFunction: Allocates the power budget toward compute by removing avoidable conversion losses along the chain.
activations.whyThisNode: The executive-control network optimizes allocation under constraint; stage reduction optimizes the power budget toward useful compute.
